name: bm-e2-actin-adhesion-collagen
title: Actin-adhesion-collagen force transfer
claim: An active cortex transmits force through reversible basal linkers to a collagen membrane patch; the transmitted traction equals linker occupancy times cortical tension (by construction, exactly), the BM strain rate is proportional to that traction, and occupancy rises toward saturation -- so the cortex -> linker -> BM force transfer is occupancy-gated.
experiment: Verify the deterministic force-transfer relation of the single-cell actin-adhesion-collagen patch (composite viva_lumenoid.composites.actin_adhesion_bm). Drive the BasalAdhesion linker process with a cortex tension of 2.0 (k_on 0.5, k_off 0.1, coupling_gain 1e-3) and read the traction, the linker occupancy and the BM strain rate; separately step the occupancy kinetics (k_off 0) to confirm it rises toward 1. Then run a bounded LAMMPS smoke of the full composite (real actomyosin cortex + collagen IV BM patch) to confirm the collagen BM responds to the transmitted load and emits its in-plane stress (bm_sigma).
result: The force-transfer relation holds exactly and deterministically. At cortex_tension 2.0 the linker occupancy is 0.5, the traction is 1.0 (= 0.5 x 2.0, exact), and the BM strain rate is 0.001 (= 1e-3 x 1.0, exact). The occupancy kinetics rise monotonically toward saturation (0.100, 0.189, 0.268, 0.339, 0.401, 0.457 over six 0.1-interval steps with k_off 0, strictly increasing toward 1). The bounded LAMMPS smoke of the full cortex+collagen composite runs the real actomyosin cortex and collagen IV BM patch end-to-end and the BM responds to the transmitted load, emitting its in-plane stress (sigma_inplane -> bm_sigma). The relations are exact because the linker process is a pure deterministic map; the result is scoped to the single-cell patch.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition: An occupancy-gated cortex -> linker -> BM force transfer that conserves the force relation exactly (traction = occupancy x tension, strain rate proportional to traction) on a single-cell patch is the force-transfer seam the multicellular / coupled-lumenoid studies build on.

question: How does active cortical contractility transfer force through reversible basal adhesions into the collagen IV basement membrane?

purpose.question: How does active cortical contractility transfer force through reversible basal adhesions into the collagen IV basement membrane, on a single-cell patch?
purpose.mechanism: An active actomyosin cortex (E1) carries a tension; reversible basal linkers with first-order on/off kinetics carry an occupancy in [0, 1]; the traction passed to the BM is occupancy x cortex_tension, which drives a BM strain rate (coupling_gain x traction) that strains and remodels the collagen IV patch beneath.
purpose.expected_outcome: A traction that is occupancy-gated (traction = occupancy x tension, exact), a BM strain rate proportional to traction, and a linker occupancy that rises toward saturation -- with the collagen BM responding to the transmitted load.

hypothesis: Coupling an active cortex to reversible basal linkers and a collagen-IV BM patch produces a traction, linker occupancy and network deformation whose relative relaxation is set jointly by linker off-rate and crosslink turnover, measurable on a single-cell patch before multicellular coupling.
objective: Couple active cortical contractility (E1) to reversible basal linkers and a collagen IV BM patch; measure traction, linker occupation, network deformation and relative relaxation; begin with a single-cell patch before multicellular coupling.
description:
The actin-adhesion-collagen force-transfer extension (plan section 5). Active cortical
contractility from E1 is coupled through reversible basal linkers (attachment sites,
occupancy, forces, work) to a collagen IV BM patch from R2. Readouts are traction, linker
occupancy, network deformation and the relative relaxation set by linker and crosslink
kinetics. A single-cell patch is validated with prescribed-displacement and imposed-traction
tests before any multicellular coupling, avoiding double-counting of BM mechanics.
key_assumptions: Reversible basal linkers follow first-order kinetics: d(occ)/dt = k_on*(1-occ) - k_off*occ, occupancy clamped to [0, 1].
Transmitted traction = linker_occupancy x cortex_tension (occupancy-gated force transfer), by construction.
BM strain rate = coupling_gain x traction (a linear traction -> deformation map).
The collagen IV BM patch (CollagenNetworkProcess) remodels under the load with its crosslink chemistry kept on (make_on/break_on).
Single-cell patch in reduced units; the linker relation is pure/deterministic (no stochasticity), so it is verified numerically rather than by a seed ensemble.

baseline.name: bm-e2-actin-adhesion-collagen
baseline.note: A single cell transferring force to its basement membrane: the actomyosin cortex pulls through reversible basal adhesions onto a collagen IV patch. The traction passed down is the fraction of bound adhesions times the cortical tension, and it strains and remodels the collagen beneath. Adhesion binding and unbinding follow simple first-order kinetics. The readouts are the traction, the fraction of bound adhesions, and the membrane's deformation.

falsifiability: The claim would be overturned if the transmitted traction did NOT equal linker occupancy times cortex tension, if the BM strain rate were not proportional to traction (coupling_gain x traction), if the linker occupancy did not rise toward saturation under binding, or if the collagen BM did not respond to (emit a stress under) the transmitted load. Because the linker relation is a pure deterministic map, any inequality in the identity checks is a hard failure. The deterministic contracts in tests/test_e2_coupling.py (test_adhesion_transmits_occupancy_gated_traction, test_adhesion_occupancy_kinetics) and the LAMMPS-gated test_e2_force_transfer_runs would fail in that case.

diagnose: Traction != occupancy x tension -- check the BasalAdhesion output wiring (occupancy clamp, tension input port).
BM does not respond -- check the collagen patch receives strain_rate/make_on/break_on and emits sigma_inplane.
if_primary_tests_fail.block_downstream: Do not advance to multicellular coupling until the single-cell force-transfer relation holds exactly.

limitations: Scope: single-cell patch only; no multicellular coupling, no prescribed-displacement / imposed-traction work-balance sweep yet.

The force-transfer relations (traction = occupancy x tension; strain rate = gain x traction) hold EXACTLY because the linker process is a pure deterministic map, not an emergent result -- the finding is that the occupancy-gated transfer is wired correctly and the BM responds.
Reduced units throughout; occupancy is a lumped fraction, not resolved attachment sites with forces/work.
The relative relaxation set jointly by linker off-rate and crosslink turnover is characterised only qualitatively (the full relaxation sweep is a follow-up).
The BM response is confirmed by a bounded LAMMPS smoke (it emits a stress under load), not a converged rheology measurement.

report.title: E2 -- actin-adhesion-collagen occupancy-gated force transfer
report.verdict: The single-cell actin-adhesion-collagen patch transmits force through reversible basal linkers with an occupancy-gated relation that holds exactly: at cortex_tension 2.0 the linker occupancy is 0.5, the traction is 1.0 (= 0.5 x 2.0), and the BM strain rate is 0.001 (= 1e-3 x 1.0). The linker occupancy rises monotonically toward saturation (0.100 -> 0.457 over six steps), and a bounded LAMMPS smoke of the full cortex+collagen composite confirms the collagen IV BM responds to the transmitted load (emits bm_sigma). The relations are exact because the linker process is a pure deterministic map; the result is scoped to a single cell.
report.main_insight: The cortex -> reversible-linker -> collagen-BM force transfer is occupancy-gated and wired correctly: the transmitted traction is exactly linker occupancy times cortical tension, the BM strain rate is proportional to traction, and the collagen BM responds -- the validated single-cell seam for multicellular coupling.
report.caveat: The force-transfer relations hold EXACTLY by construction (a deterministic map), not as an emergent result; the BM response is a bounded smoke, not a converged rheology measurement; single-cell patch in reduced units only.

findings.statement: The active cortex transmits force to the collagen BM through an occupancy-gated relation: the traction equals linker occupancy times cortex tension exactly (1.0 = 0.5 x 2.0 at cortex_tension 2.0), so the fraction of bound basal linkers sets how much cortical tension reaches the membrane.

expected.summary: cortical tension reaches the BM gated by the fraction of engaged basal adhesions (occupancy-gated force transfer)

findings.explanation: BasalAdhesion carries a lumped occupancy with first-order on/off kinetics and returns traction = occupancy x tension; the relation is exact by construction, confirming the cortex -> linker -> BM wiring transmits force only through engaged linkers.
findings.next_action: advance the validated single-cell seam to multicellular / coupled-lumenoid force transfer

findings.statement: The BM strain rate is proportional to the transmitted traction (0.001 = 1e-3 x 1.0, exact), the linker occupancy rises monotonically toward saturation (0.100 -> 0.457 over six steps), and a bounded LAMMPS smoke of the full cortex+collagen composite confirms the collagen IV BM responds to the load by emitting its in-plane stress (bm_sigma).

evidence.observed: bm_strain_rate 0.001 == coupling_gain 1e-3 x traction 1.0; occupancy 0.100->0.457; full composite emits sigma_inplane -> bm_sigma

findings.explanation: coupling_gain linearly maps traction to BM strain rate; the collagen patch receives the strain rate (with crosslink chemistry on) and reports a stress, closing the cortex -> linker -> BM chain.

followup_proposals.title: Prescribed-displacement / imposed-traction work balance and the linker+crosslink relaxation sweep
followup_proposals.motivation: This study verifies the occupancy-gated force-transfer relation and confirms the BM responds, but not the work balance across the cortex -> adhesion -> BM chain nor the relative relaxation set jointly by linker off-rate and crosslink turnover. Add prescribed-displacement and imposed-traction tests and sweep k_off x crosslink turnover.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: The relative relaxation of occupancy vs BM deformation should be set by the ratio of linker off-rate to crosslink turnover time.

resolved_uncertainties: The cortex -> linker -> BM force transfer is occupancy-gated and wired correctly (traction = occupancy x tension, exact).
The BM strain rate is proportional to traction, and the collagen IV BM responds to the transmitted load.
remaining_uncertainties: The work balance across the cortex -> adhesion -> BM chain (prescribed-displacement / imposed-traction tests).
The relative relaxation set jointly by linker off-rate and crosslink turnover.
Whether the single-cell relation survives multicellular coupling without double-counting BM mechanics.

regression_compatibility.basis: The actin_adhesion_bm composite is registered and the cortex -> linker -> BM chain runs cleanly; the deterministic contracts in tests/test_e2_coupling.py pass, and the LAMMPS-gated full-chain smoke runs with LAMMPS installed.

biological_validation.basis: Occupancy-gated force transfer holds by construction (traction = occupancy x tension, exact) and the collagen BM responds to the transmitted load. The relations being exact (a deterministic map) rather than emergent is noted as a limitation.

explanatory_gain.basis: Establishes the validated single-cell force-transfer seam (cortex -> reversible linkers -> collagen BM) that multicellular / coupled-lumenoid studies build on, a NEW extension beyond the paper.

expert_questions: Fidelity: the linker is a lumped occupancy (traction = occupancy x tension) rather than resolved attachment sites with forces/work. Is the lumped relation sufficient for the force-transfer seam, or should the single-cell patch resolve per-linker forces before multicellular coupling?

Relaxation: should the canonical E2 run include the prescribed-displacement / imposed-traction work-balance tests and the linker-off-rate x crosslink-turnover relaxation sweep before the force-transfer is called complete?
